meta.title: Bumimic — an open recorder for listening to nature
meta.description: A low-cost, open acoustic recorder for biodiversity monitoring. The first prototype units arrive in mid-September.

hero.title: Bumimic
hero.lede: A low-cost, open recorder that listens to a place around the clock, keeps the audio on a memory card, and sends short alerts back over long-range radio.
hero.imageAlt: Misty forest landscape at first light

prototype.title: Not for sale yet
prototype.body: Bumimic is a working prototype. The first units arrive in mid-September for field testing, and the design still has to pass sound, radio, power and safety checks before anyone can order one.

record.title: Records around the clock
record.body: Up to 384,000 samples a second in 16-bit, with a half-rate mode when a longer deployment matters more than the highest frequencies. Audio is written straight to a microSD card.

sense.title: Reads its surroundings
sense.body: Temperature, humidity, light, air pressure and movement are recorded alongside the sound, so every detection arrives with the conditions that produced it.

radio.title: Sends short alerts home
radio.body: Detections and battery health travel back over long-range radio, so a site can be checked without visiting it. The recordings themselves stay on the card.

power.title: Runs on ordinary batteries
power.body: Three AA or AAA cells, with USB-C for setup. Between recordings the board is designed to draw only a few millionths of an amp.

board.title: The prototype board
board.body: The design is open from the start: schematic, board layout, manufacturing files and firmware are all developed in public so field teams can build, repair and adapt it themselves.
board.caption: Bumimic prototype board, 57 × 47 mm — slightly smaller than an AudioMoth in both directions.
board.imageAlt: Render of the Bumimic prototype circuit board, showing the microSD slot, radio module and sensors
board.repoPending: The design files will be published once the prototype has been through field testing.

cost.title: What we expect it to cost

board.label: Board and assembly
board.note: Electronics and assembly at a run of about 1,000 units.

unit.label: Complete field unit
unit.note: All the electronics for a deployable recorder, before enclosure and batteries.

cost.note: These are planning estimates, not supplier quotes. Real prices depend on the configuration, the country it ships to, and what manufacturers quote when we order.

regions.title: Built for a specific place
regions.body: Radio rules differ from country to country, so each unit is built and labelled for where it will be deployed. The first builds target these three.

cta.title: Interested in Bumimic?
cta.description: Tell us about your site and how you would use a recorder there. We are looking for field teams to test the first units with.
